entries.requirement: Before claiming any feature/wave done, run it in Dolphin (local or headless) and produce screenshot evidence -- reasoning about the change is not sufficient.
entries.why: E2E Verification Gate, part of the always-loaded core-safety standard.

entries.requirement: Never allocate memory per-frame; allocate once at init and reuse, on hardware with only ~24MB MEM1.
entries.why: Inviolable Rule #4 of core-safety: OOM after hours of gameplay is caused by per-frame malloc on constrained Wii memory.

entries.requirement: After creating any new .c file, grep for the filename in the Makefile; if missing, add it before claiming the work done.
entries.why: Makefile Gate in core-safety's Build & Integration Gates -- a new source file that is never compiled is a silent no-op.

entries.requirement: After expanding any enum with a _MAX/_COUNT sentinel, grep for ENUM_MAX across source/ and include/ and verify every array indexed by that enum was resized to match, or it is an out-of-bounds read / UB / crash.
entries.why: Enum Sync Gate in core-safety's Build & Integration Gates.

entries.requirement: Textures and vertex buffers that GX reads must be allocated with memalign(32, size) and cache-flushed with DCFlushRange(buf, size) before GX reads them; never malloc GX-visible data.
entries.why: malloc is not guaranteed 32-byte aligned -- it works in Dolphin (which is lenient) but fails on real Wii hardware, a documented Dolphin-vs-hardware divergence.

origin.quote: **Textures/vertex buffers:** `memalign(32, size)` + `DCFlushRange(buf, size)` before GX reads. Never `malloc` for GX data (not guaranteed 32-byte aligned; works in Dolphin, fails on Wii).

entries.requirement: Never include POSIX-only headers such as <unistd.h> or <pthread.h> -- Wii has no POSIX layer.

entries.requirement: A runtime claim (it boots, it works, it renders) must name the plane that observed it (static/Dolphin/silicon); an unattributed claim is not a claim.
entries.why: The development plane optimizes engineering speed; the validation plane owns every runtime verdict -- conflating them lets an unproven claim pass as proven.

origin.quote: > every runtime verdict. A claim names the plane that observed it, or it is not a claim.**

entries.requirement: When verifying a claim about Wii runtime behavior, rank evidence by authority (silicon > gex44/live-device-bot > emulator > binary/disassembly > static source > documentation > inference) and resolve contradictions by authority, never by counting how many sources agree.
entries.why: Five agents reading one wrong corpus agree perfectly -- a majority vote among same-provenance sources is not independent evidence.

origin.quote: `silicon > gex44 > emulator > binary/disassembly > static source > documentation > inference`
